chapter: Benny Goodman, Basie and the swing era
title: Upcoming dates with Clooney and Henderson, and White House performances
summary: His coming engagements, Victor Young's score played 40 years on, and two White House performances.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well next week I’m playing with Rosemary Clooney, two weeks at the Rainbow Room. And I’m doing a concert with John. I’m doing a couple of symphony dates with Skitch Henderson in Florida, in Tampa, four dates — Clearwater, St. Petersburg, Tampa. I get a big kick out of doing that too. I’m playing things that I used to listen to on record, a score by Victor Young called “For Whom The Bell Tolls.” It’s something that we all used to listen to when we were young: listen to this — and listen to this. And the record was worn out in one spot. And 40 years later I’m playing the same tune.
So you know it’s a big kick. And it’s something I didn’t push, but there I am. I did it three weeks ago with Skitch at Carnegie Hall.
You played at the White House a number of times?
I played there twice. Once with Benny Goodman and Buddy Rich and Milt Hinton, Hank Jones.
And the second time was with Sinatra, with just a small group. Tony Mottola, myself.
